title: Impact of Merit Scholarships on College Enrollment

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
The appropriate causal method for this scenario is Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD). We use RDD because we are interested in the causal impact of meeting a specific GPA threshold on college enrollment. The treatment is determined by whether students' GPA is above or below the cutoff. The key assumption is that students just above and just below the cutoff are similar in all respects except for the receipt of the scholarship, ensuring local randomization at the threshold.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(rdd)

# Load the dataset
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s85_data.csv")

# Basic summary of dataset
summary(data)

# Running the RDD analysis
rdd_data <- rdd_data(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, cutpoint = 0.5)

# Fitting the RDD model
rdd_model <- rdd_reg_lm(rdd_object = rdd_data)

# Summary of the model to see the treatment effect at the threshold
summary(rdd_model)

# Printing the estimated treatment effect
cat("Estimated treatment effect at the cutoff: ", rdd_model$coefficients[2], "\n")

# Plot the RDD
plot_rdd(rdd_model)

# Robustness Checks: Using a smaller bandwidth
rdd_model_bw <- rdd_reg_lm(rdd_object = rdd_data, bw = 0.1)
summary(rdd_model_bw)

# Printing the estimated treatment effect using smaller bandwidth
cat("Estimated treatment effect at the cutoff with smaller bandwidth: ", rdd_model_bw$coefficients[2], "\n")

# Plot the RDD with smaller bandwidth
plot_rdd(rdd_model_bw)
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive treatment effect, meaning that meeting the GPA threshold for the merit scholarship will increase college enrollment rates. The intuition is that the availability of financial support will likely reduce the cost burden of attending college, thus incentivizing students to enroll. The magnitude of the effect will depend on the baseline enrollment rate and the financial significance of the scholarship. I would anticipate a modest to moderate positive effect, as financial incentives are a significant factor in education decisions.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: The analysis exploits the GPA threshold as a cutoff to compare students just above and below the threshold.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Meeting the GPA threshold for a merit scholarship significantly increases college enrollment rates.
